headline: Direct conversions jumped 3.6x on flat spend alongside a rise in AI-assistant self-reports, so no paid channel should get the credit and no budgets move this week.

tests.hypothesis: Part of Google's reported gain (240 to ~400 conversions/week on flat ~$4.2k spend) is branded search catching demand created by AI assistants, so true incremental ROAS is below the 18x reported.
tests.design: Geo holdout: pause brand-term campaigns in ~20% of matched regions for 4 weeks, keep non-brand running. Measure total conversions (Google + direct + email) in held-out vs control regions, plus the share of buyers answering 'Google' vs 'ChatGPT/AI assistant' in the post-purchase survey. Do not change budgets elsewhere during the test.

flag_verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Direct went from 5.7 to 20.7/day (weekly 33 to 152) with paid spend flat at 1.00x. Self-reported 'AI assistant' plus 'Asked ChatGPT' rose from about 16% (Aug 3 week) to 41% (Oct 26 week). Untracked AI-driven demand is the likely cause. Action: no budget moves and a holdout test on Google, because Google's reported gains may be capturing the same demand.

flags.message: Direct conversions grew 3.6x (5.7 to 20.7/day) while paid spend moved 1.00x. Self-reported AI answers went from 18% to 37%. Something untracked is driving buyers.

label: synthetic data
